newsitem.title: UK: Embattled British pro-Europeans launch fightback.
newsitem.headline: Embattled British pro-Europeans launch fightback.

text.p: A lobby group on Thursday launched a fightback against people who have raised the prospect of Britain pulling out of the European Union, warning that such a move would put thousands of jobs at risk.

Businessmen, a trade union leader and MPs from the three main political parties held a joint news conference under the auspices of the European Movement to voice their alarm at the tone of the debate on Europe in Britain.

The organisation plans to distribute a tabloid newspaper detailing dozens of benefits it says Britain derives from membership of the 15-nation bloc to a million British homes, and to take advertising space in newspapers.

Its two central messages are that the EU has boosted Britain's economy by giving it a huge home market and enabling it to attract foreign investment, and that it has led to the longest period of peace in Western Europe for 300 years.

"This campaign shows just how overwhelming the benefits of Europe have been. There is no question that we are better off in -- and that's where we should stay," Sir Leon Brittan, one of Britain's EU commissioners, told the news conference.

Giles Radice, a Labour MP who is chairman of the European Movement, said the campaign was needed because of "a tirade of (anti-European) criticism and propaganda by politicians and much of the media".

Some British newspapers and politicians have been taking an increasingly hostile stance towards Brussels in recent months, claiming the EU is moving towards a federal superstate which would reduce Britain to the status of a province.

But Edwina Currie, a pro-European Conservative MP with a constituency in the Midlands region of central England, said: "Any suggestion that we should start pulling out, or that Britain would do well outside Europe, is in my view completely nuts".
"Ten thousand jobs in my constituency would be at risk and that would be replicated throughout the Midlands."
"I find it hard to believe that my party has anybody in it who wants to turn their back and walk away. I find it quite incredible."
